title: Breast Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for breast cancer. Full pathway by histology (DCIS, invasive, inflammatory, phyllodes, Paget, pregnancy, recurrent/Stage IV), then workup -> local-regional vs preoperative-systemic -> subtype-directed adjuvant (HR/HER2) -> adjuvant endocrine (pre/post-menopausal) -> surveillance, plus recurrent / metastatic treatment by subtype and local/regional recurrence. Each treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; surgery / radiation and agents without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup / staging / subtype-stratification content is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text; structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Breast Cancer, no proprietary content reproduced. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Breast Cancer. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Breast cancer type
nodes.description: Breast cancer management branches first by disease type / presentation. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)
Invasive breast cancer (non-metastatic)
Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC)
Phyllodes tumor
Paget disease of the nipple
Breast cancer during pregnancy
Recurrent or Stage IV (metastatic) disease

nodes.name: DCIS workup
nodes.title: DCIS: workup
nodes.description: Non-invasive disease confined to the ducts. Confirm no invasion and establish ER status.
bullets: History and physical; diagnostic bilateral mammography
Core biopsy confirming DCIS (rule out invasion); pathology review
Estrogen-receptor (ER) status on the DCIS
Breast MRI in selected cases; genetic counseling if criteria met

nodes.name: DCIS ER status
nodes.title: DCIS: estrogen-receptor status
nodes.description: ER status determines whether endocrine risk-reduction is offered after local therapy.

nodes.name: DCIS ER+
nodes.title: DCIS, ER-positive: local therapy + endocrine risk-reduction
nodes.description: Local therapy with optional endocrine risk-reduction.
bullets: Lumpectomy + whole-breast radiation, OR total mastectomy (no axillary staging for pure DCIS)
Endocrine risk-reduction: tamoxifen (pre/post-menopausal) or an aromatase inhibitor (postmenopausal) for breast-conserving therapy
Endocrine agent regimens referenced below

nodes.name: DCIS ER-
nodes.title: DCIS, ER-negative: local therapy
nodes.description: Local therapy; endocrine therapy is not indicated.
bullets: Lumpectomy + whole-breast radiation, OR total mastectomy
No endocrine therapy (ER-negative)
Surveillance with annual mammography

nodes.name: Invasive workup
nodes.title: Invasive: clinical stage and workup
nodes.description: Establish clinical stage and tumor biology to plan sequencing of surgery and systemic therapy.
bullets: History and physical; bilateral diagnostic mammography +/- breast MRI
Core biopsy: ER, PR, HER2, and histologic grade; consider Ki-67
Clinical staging (cTNM); systemic staging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis + bone scan, or PET-CT) for stage III / node-positive / symptoms
Germline testing (BRCA1/2 and panel) if criteria met; fertility counseling in premenopausal patients
Assess menopausal status; baseline cardiac function if anthracycline / HER2 therapy planned

nodes.name: Sequencing
nodes.title: Invasive: upfront surgery vs preoperative systemic therapy
nodes.description: Choose primary sequencing. Preoperative (neoadjuvant) systemic therapy is preferred for HER2-positive or triple-negative tumors >= T2 or node-positive, and to downstage large / locally advanced or inoperable tumors.

nodes.name: Locoregional
nodes.title: Locoregional treatment (cT1-3, cN0 or N+, M0)
nodes.description: Definitive local-regional therapy; then subtype-directed adjuvant systemic therapy.
bullets: Breast-conserving surgery + whole-breast radiation (BCS + RT) for suitable tumor:breast ratio
Total mastectomy +/- post-mastectomy radiation (PMRT) for T3-4, node-positive, or patient choice
Axillary staging: sentinel-node biopsy; axillary dissection for proven node-positive disease

nodes.name: BCS + RT
nodes.title: Breast-conserving surgery + whole-breast RT
nodes.description: Breast conservation with radiation, then subtype-directed adjuvant systemic therapy.
bullets: Lumpectomy to negative margins (no ink on tumor) + surgical axillary staging (sentinel-node biopsy; axillary dissection if node-positive)
Whole-breast radiation; boost to the tumor bed for high-risk features
Accelerated / partial-breast irradiation (APBI/PBI) for appropriately selected low-risk patients
Omission of radiation may be considered in selected older patients with low-risk, ER-positive tumors on endocrine therapy
Then subtype-directed adjuvant systemic therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Mastectomy +/- PMRT
nodes.title: Total mastectomy +/- post-mastectomy RT (PMRT)
nodes.description: Mastectomy with post-mastectomy radiation as indicated by nodal status / tumor stage / margins, then adjuvant systemic therapy.
bullets: Total mastectomy +/- reconstruction + surgical axillary staging (sentinel-node biopsy; axillary dissection if node-positive)
PMRT (+ regional nodal irradiation) for node-positive disease, T3-4 tumors, or positive margins
PMRT generally not required for node-negative, <= T2, negative-margin (>= 1 mm) disease
Consider PMRT for node-negative disease with multiple high-risk features (young age, LVI, grade 3, ER-negative)
Then subtype-directed adjuvant systemic therapy (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant systemic
nodes.title: Preoperative (neoadjuvant) systemic therapy
nodes.description: Neoadjuvant systemic therapy matched to subtype, then surgery, then adjuvant. Regimen is chosen by subtype (see the subtype step next).
bullets: HER2-positive: chemotherapy + HER2 blockade (e.g. TCHP / trastuzumab + pertuzumab based)
Triple-negative: anthracycline + taxane + carboplatin, with pembrolizumab for high-risk / node-positive
HR-positive/HER2-negative: anthracycline / taxane chemotherapy for high-risk disease (or neoadjuvant endocrine in selected postmenopausal patients)
Then surgery (BCS or mastectomy) with response assessment; residual disease guides adjuvant escalation
Component regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant after neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Adjuvant therapy after preoperative systemic therapy + surgery
nodes.description: After neoadjuvant therapy and surgery, adjuvant therapy is guided by residual disease and subtype.
bullets: HER2-positive with residual disease: switch to T-DM1 (trastuzumab emtansine)
Triple-negative with residual disease: consider capecitabine (and continue pembrolizumab if started)
HR-positive: complete adjuvant endocrine therapy; add olaparib for germline BRCA / high-risk HER2-negative
Radiation as indicated by surgery and nodal status

nodes.name: Receptor subtype
nodes.title: Adjuvant systemic therapy: receptor subtype
nodes.description: Adjuvant systemic therapy is directed by hormone-receptor (HR = ER/PR) and HER2 status.

nodes.name: HR+/HER2- menopausal
nodes.title: Adjuvant HR-positive / HER2-negative: menopausal status
nodes.description: For HR-positive / HER2-negative disease, adjuvant chemotherapy selection and endocrine therapy differ by menopausal status (and, in premenopausal patients, nodal status).

nodes.name: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- postmeno
nodes.title: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- (postmenopausal)
nodes.description: Chemotherapy is selected by a genomic-recurrence assay plus clinical risk; endocrine therapy for all.
bullets: Genomic assay (e.g. 21-gene recurrence score) guides who benefits from chemotherapy
Chemotherapy (e.g. TC, or anthracycline + taxane) for high genomic / clinical risk
Adjuvant endocrine therapy for all (aromatase-inhibitor based - see next step)
Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib) for high-risk node-positive disease; olaparib for germline BRCA
Chemotherapy regimens referenced below

nodes.name: HR+/HER2- premeno nodal
nodes.title: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- (premenopausal): nodal status
nodes.description: In premenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative disease, chemotherapy decisions differ by pathologic nodal status.

nodes.name: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- premeno pN0
nodes.title: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- (premenopausal, node-negative)
nodes.description: Genomic-assay-guided chemotherapy; endocrine therapy for all.
bullets: Genomic assay (e.g. 21-gene recurrence score) guides chemotherapy benefit; most low-score node-negative patients can omit chemotherapy
Chemotherapy (e.g. TC or AC-T) for high recurrence score / high clinical risk
Adjuvant endocrine therapy for all - tamoxifen, or ovarian suppression + an AI / tamoxifen for higher risk (see next step)
Chemotherapy regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- premeno pN+
nodes.title: Adjuvant HR+/HER2- (premenopausal, node-positive)
nodes.description: Chemotherapy is generally recommended, followed by ovarian-suppression-based endocrine therapy.
bullets: Adjuvant chemotherapy (anthracycline + taxane, e.g. dose-dense AC-T) is generally recommended
Then endocrine therapy with ovarian function suppression + an AI or tamoxifen (see next step)
Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib) for high-risk node-positive disease; olaparib for germline BRCA
Chemotherapy regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant HR+/HER2+
nodes.title: Adjuvant: HR-positive / HER2-positive
nodes.description: Chemotherapy + HER2-targeted therapy, followed by endocrine therapy.
bullets: Chemotherapy + trastuzumab (+ pertuzumab for node-positive): TCH / TCHP or AC followed by paclitaxel + trastuzumab
Complete 1 year of HER2-targeted therapy; T-DM1 if residual disease after neoadjuvant
Then adjuvant endocrine therapy (see next step)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant HR-/HER2+
nodes.title: Adjuvant: HR-negative / HER2-positive
nodes.description: Chemotherapy + HER2-targeted therapy (no endocrine therapy).
bullets: Chemotherapy + trastuzumab (+ pertuzumab for node-positive): TCH / TCHP or AC then paclitaxel + trastuzumab
Complete 1 year of HER2-targeted therapy; T-DM1 if residual disease after neoadjuvant
No endocrine therapy (HR-negative)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Adjuvant TNBC
nodes.title: Adjuvant: triple-negative
nodes.description: Chemotherapy-based; immunotherapy for higher-stage disease.
bullets: Anthracycline + taxane (+ carboplatin) chemotherapy
Add pembrolizumab (neoadjuvant + adjuvant) for stage II-III disease
Capecitabine for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
Add olaparib for germline BRCA-mutated high-risk disease
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Favorable histology
nodes.title: Adjuvant: favorable histology (tubular / mucinous)
nodes.description: Favorable histologies are usually ER-positive with excellent prognosis.
bullets: Endocrine therapy if ER-positive (see next step); chemotherapy rarely needed
Treat as triple-negative if ER-negative (uncommon for these histologies)

nodes.name: Adjuvant endocrine
nodes.title: Adjuvant endocrine therapy: menopausal status
nodes.description: For HR-positive disease, adjuvant endocrine therapy is directed by menopausal status.

nodes.name: Endocrine postmenopausal
nodes.title: Adjuvant endocrine (postmenopausal) +/- CDK4/6
nodes.description: Aromatase-inhibitor-based endocrine therapy.
bullets: An aromatase inhibitor (letrozole, anastrozole, or exemestane) for 5-10 years; tamoxifen if AI not tolerated
Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib) for high-risk node-positive disease
Bone-health monitoring on an AI (DEXA, calcium/vitamin D, bone-modifying agent as indicated)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Endocrine premenopausal
nodes.title: Adjuvant endocrine (premenopausal) +/- OFS / CDK4/6
nodes.description: Tamoxifen, or ovarian suppression with an AI/tamoxifen for higher risk.
bullets: Tamoxifen for 5-10 years
Ovarian function suppression + an AI or tamoxifen for higher-risk disease
Add a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib) for high-risk node-positive disease
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy.
bullets: History and physical every 3-6 months for 5 years, then annually
Annual mammography (of preserved / contralateral breast)
Endocrine-therapy adherence and toxicity review; bone-health on an AI
No routine systemic imaging or tumor markers in asymptomatic patients; investigate new symptoms

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrent / Stage IV: type of recurrence
nodes.description: Distinguish isolated local-regional recurrence (potentially curable) from distant metastatic disease.
bullets: Biopsy the recurrence and re-test ER, PR, and HER2 (receptors can change)
Restage to exclude distant disease (CT + bone scan, or PET-CT)

nodes.name: Local recurrence
nodes.title: Treatment of local recurrence
nodes.description: Isolated local recurrence is treated with curative intent.
bullets: Surgical resection (mastectomy if prior BCS; re-excision if prior mastectomy)
Radiation to the chest wall / breast if not previously given
Systemic therapy directed by the recurrence subtype (see distant-metastatic options)

nodes.name: Regional recurrence
nodes.title: Treatment of regional (nodal) recurrence
nodes.description: Isolated regional nodal recurrence.
bullets: Surgical resection of resectable nodal disease
Radiation to the regional nodal basin if not previously given
Systemic therapy directed by the recurrence subtype (see distant-metastatic options)

nodes.name: Metastatic subtype
nodes.title: Metastatic breast cancer: subtype
nodes.description: First-line metastatic therapy is directed by receptor subtype (re-biopsied). Test germline BRCA and, for triple-negative, PD-L1.

nodes.name: Metastatic HR+ line
nodes.title: Metastatic HR+/HER2-: line of therapy
nodes.description: Endocrine-based therapy is preferred while endocrine-sensitive; sequencing depends on prior therapy and biomarkers (PIK3CA/AKT/PTEN, ESR1, germline BRCA).

nodes.name: Metastatic HR+ 1st line
nodes.title: Metastatic HR+/HER2-: first line
nodes.description: Endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor.
bullets: Aromatase inhibitor (or fulvestrant) + a CDK4/6 inhibitor (category 1)
Ovarian suppression added for premenopausal patients
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic HR+ 2nd line
nodes.title: Metastatic HR+/HER2-: after CDK4/6 (biomarker-directed)
nodes.description: Biomarker-directed endocrine + targeted therapy after progression on endocrine + CDK4/6.
bullets: PIK3CA/AKT/PTEN-altered: fulvestrant + a PI3K/AKT inhibitor (alpelisib or capivasertib)
ESR1-mutant: elacestrant (an oral SERD)
Germline BRCA: a PARP inhibitor (olaparib or talazoparib)
Otherwise: fulvestrant +/- everolimus, or an alternate endocrine + targeted combination
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic HR+ refractory
nodes.title: Metastatic HR+/HER2-: endocrine-refractory / visceral crisis
nodes.description: Cytotoxic therapy and antibody-drug conjugates once endocrine-refractory.
bullets: Sequential single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. capecitabine, taxane)
Antibody-drug conjugates: sacituzumab govitecan, or trastuzumab deruxtecan if HER2-low (guidance where no dose protocol exists here)
Chemotherapy for visceral crisis regardless of endocrine sensitivity
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic HER2+
nodes.title: Metastatic HER2-positive
nodes.description: Sequential HER2-targeted therapy.
bullets: First line: taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (THP)
Second line: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)
Later: tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine, T-DM1, or other HER2-directed regimens
Add endocrine therapy if also HR-positive
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic TNBC
nodes.title: Metastatic triple-negative
nodes.description: Biomarker-directed chemotherapy / immunotherapy.
bullets: PD-L1-positive: chemotherapy + pembrolizumab first line
Sacituzumab govitecan after prior chemotherapy (no dedicated dose protocol here yet - guidance)
Olaparib / talazoparib for germline BRCA
Single-agent chemotherapy (e.g. capecitabine, taxane) otherwise
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Inflammatory BC
nodes.title: Inflammatory breast cancer: trimodality therapy
nodes.description: Inflammatory breast cancer is treated as locally advanced disease with preoperative systemic therapy, then surgery, then radiation.
bullets: Preoperative systemic therapy: anthracycline + taxane, with HER2 blockade if HER2-positive and pembrolizumab if triple-negative
Then total mastectomy + axillary dissection (no breast conservation, no upfront sentinel-node biopsy)
Then post-mastectomy radiation to chest wall and regional nodes
Adjuvant endocrine / HER2 therapy by subtype
Component regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Phyllodes
nodes.title: Phyllodes tumor: wide local excision
nodes.description: A fibroepithelial tumor managed surgically.
bullets: Wide local excision with >= 1 cm negative margins (mastectomy if needed for margins)
No routine axillary staging (spreads hematogenously, not via nodes)
No routine endocrine or HER2 therapy; chemotherapy only for selected large malignant tumors (sarcoma-type)
Consider radiation for large / malignant tumors or close margins

nodes.name: Paget disease
nodes.title: Paget disease: treat the underlying cancer
nodes.description: Nipple Paget disease usually overlies underlying DCIS or invasive cancer.
bullets: Breast MRI to define underlying disease extent
Surgery: central lumpectomy (including nipple-areola) + radiation, or mastectomy
Axillary staging and adjuvant systemic therapy per the underlying invasive component / subtype

nodes.name: During pregnancy
nodes.title: Breast cancer during pregnancy
nodes.description: Stage-appropriate treatment timed to protect the fetus; coordinate with maternal-fetal medicine.
bullets: Surgery can be done in any trimester; sentinel-node biopsy is generally acceptable
Chemotherapy (anthracycline + taxane) only after the first trimester
NO endocrine therapy, HER2-targeted therapy, or radiation during pregnancy - defer to after delivery
Deliver at term when feasible, then complete stage-appropriate adjuvant therapy
Chemotherapy regimen referenced below
